item.title: 🎙 Comment (full text) by Ambassador Stepanov to The Canadian Press News Agency on recent Prime-Minister Mark Carney’s
item.description: 🎙 Comment (full text) by Ambassador Stepanov to The Canadian Press News Agency on recent Prime-Minister Mark Carney’s remarks regarding Russian and Belorussian Hockey Athletes (Ottawa, November 4, 2026) ❗️ It is genuinely regrettable to see Prime Minister Carney’s Cabinet bringing politics onto the ice. Sport, particularly junior hockey, should be about athletic excellence, fair competition and bringing young people together . Of course, one cannot help admiring the remarkable convenience of this particular display of political principle. By excluding Russian and Belorussian players, the Canadian government also happens to eliminate some rather formidable competitors before the first puck is even dropped . One might almost suspect that Ottawa has discovered a novel approach to winning international tournaments. ☝️ If you cannot be entirely certain of beating your strongest opponents on the ice, simply ensure they never make it to the rink. A splendid strategy, perhaps, for securing a trophy. A rather less splendid one for preserving the spirit of sport.

#UnityDay

#OTD
Russia commemorates
the liberation of Moscow from Polish-Lithuanian forces in 1612
– a turning point in overcoming the Time of Troubles, one of the darkest chapters in the country’s history.
At the heart of this struggle for the future of the entire nation was
the Second People’s Militia
, raised in Nizhny Novgorod under the leadership of
Kuzma Minin
and commanded by
Prince Dmitry Pozharsky
.
Following the collapse of the First People’s Militia, a new volunteer force began to assemble in the autumn of 1611. Inspired by
Patriarch Hermogen’s
call to defend the Orthodox faith and the Motherland
, the people of Nizhny Novgorod rallied around Minin, contributing money, weapons and supplies. Nobles, merchants, Cossacks, townspeople and peasants joined a common cause:
to free their country from foreign invaders and occupation
.
⚔️
By late summer 1612,
the militia had reached Moscow
, where the Polish-Lithuanian garrison held the Kremlin and Kitay-Gorod. Together with other Russian forces, it defeated a relief army led by
Hetman Jan Karol Chodkiewicz
, preventing vital supplies and reinforcements from reaching the besieged garrison.
The decisive breakthrough came in the autumn.
Russian forces stormed Kitay-Gorod
, leaving the occupiers confined to the Kremlin. Cut off from relief and weakened by hunger, the remaining garrison surrendered soon afterwards.
☝️
Moscow was liberated.
This victory paved the way for the restoration of Russian state authority. In 1613, the
Zemsky Sobor elected Mikhail Romanov as Tsar
, establishing a dynasty that would rule for more than three centuries.

years on, the triumph of 1612 remains a symbol of national unity, courage and the Russian people’s determination to defend their homeland.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33213

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answer to a media question
on the situation on the Korean Peninsula
(November 3, 2026)
❓
Question: Tensions on the Korean Peninsula, including around the Demilitarised Zone, have escalated sharply, and Seoul is once again trying to shift the blame onto Pyongyang. How do you see the situation in this subregion developing?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
Regrettably, the situation on the Korean Peninsula shows
no sign of stabilising
and
continues to deteriorate
.
Of particular concern is that the situation is deteriorating amid
ongoing large-scale military exercises
conducted by the US and the Republic of Korea near the DPRK border.
These manoeuvres are overtly provocative
. By the participants’ own admission, they are designed to rehearse
pre-emptive strikes against the DPRK
, including with nuclear weapons.
☝️
These exercises are growing in frequency and scale
and now extend across land, air, maritime and cyber domains.
For example, October saw
the US-ROK Iron Mace command-post exercise
, which involved rehearsing scenarios for the deployment of US strategic assets to the Korean Peninsula;
the ROK Armed Forces’ Hoguk exercise
;
US military training in airborne operations
behind the lines of a simulated adversary; and the second round this year of
the joint US-ROK Freedom Flag air exercise
, which is scheduled to continue until November 6. In addition, Seoul, Washington and Tokyo practised combat interoperability during
the trilateral, multidomain Freedom Edge exercises
held in September.
❗️
In these circumstances, we regard the measures Pyongyang is taking to strengthen its security and defence capabilities as
entirely lawful and justified
, in full accordance with
the right to self-defence
enshrined in
the UN Charter
.
We urge Seoul to immediately cease its dangerous military games and provocations
, particularly in the Demilitarised Zone, rather than seeking far-fetched pretexts for accusing the DPRK or making empty declarations about peace, and
to respect Pyongyang’s sovereign right to ensure its own security by all means available
.

🎙
Remarks
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the High-Level Plenary Session of the Fourth Minsk International Conference on Eurasian Security
(Minsk, November 3, 2026)
Key points
:
• Honest, open discussions on ensuring reliable and lasting Eurasian security – an issue of importance to us all –
are more vital today than ever
. This is particularly true given the
#GlobalMajority
’s clear demand for
a new model of world order
.
•
Russia supports the emergence of a just system of international relations based on
#Multipolarity
. It must reflect the cultural and civilisational diversity of the modern world and its peoples, recognising each people’s right to determine their own destiny.
•
We are consistently working to advance President Vladimir Putin’s initiative to establish
a Greater Eurasian Partnership
, put forward back at
the First #RussiaASEAN Summit
, by building ties between integration associations across Eurasia. This process is already underway, involving the
#EAEU
,
#SCO
and
#ASEAN
.
• Attempts to ensure the practical implementation of the principle of equal and indivisible security
within the Euro-Atlantic
– specifically Euro-Atlantic, rather than Eurasian –
security framework have
failed
. The West proved
unwilling to cooperate
on an honest and equal footing.
•
The OSCE’s current state is frankly deplorable
. This is the result of the same confrontational logic of bloc mentality pursued by Western countries.
• Does the OSCE have a future when its history symbolises the failure of the Euro-Atlantic security model? Rooted in the illusions of the late Cold War era,
this model requires a fundamental overhaul if it is to remain viable
. Yet what we hear from Brussels are calls to build
a system of “European security” without Russia and Belarus
– or, frankly speaking,
directed against our two countries
.
•
Today, we call for indivisible security through the development of a pan-Eurasian
, rather than Euro-Atlantic,
architecture
, open to all countries and associations on the continent and reflecting the realities of a
#MultipolarWorld
.
• Commitment to the principles of indivisible security, openness and equality means that
countries harbour no hostile intentions towards one another or towards third countries
. This could involve developing
a system of mutual and cross-cutting security guarantees
at both bilateral and multilateral levels.
• We believe that the framework document –
the Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the 21st Century
– should help consolidate
a continent-wide consensus
on the foundations of such cooperation.

an alternative short draft resolution
to the Security Council that
would have extended the Mission’s mandate for one year without any changes

The US voted against it
, while the remaining members abstained.
☝️
As a result, our proposal was not adopted.
We believe that
full responsibility
for winding down the UN presence in Western Sahara, which has long had a stabilising effect on the situation in the region,
lies with the US and the countries that sided with it.
